result.summary: Optimizes peer address grouping and ASMap lookups in AddrMan by eliminating unnecessary heap allocations, redundant network classifications, and integer decoding overhead. When ASMap is disabled or empty, GetMappedAS returns early without re-classifying the address; with ASMap enabled, lookup keys are constructed on the stack and vector capacity for group tags is pre-reserved. The PR also adds microbenchmarks and unit tests covering ASN byte-order and IPv4-mapped address variants.
result.problem: AddrMan groups peer addresses frequently, but without ASMap configured it redundantly classifies each address twice. When ASMap is active, each lookup allocates a temporary key on the heap, repeatedly calculates mantissa shift distances during integer decoding, and triggers multiple reallocations when building the small group byte vector.
evidence: Author microbenchmarks on a Raspberry Pi 5 show AddrManAdd running 19.2% faster overall (59.1 ms to 49.6 ms) across the patch set (PR description).

Individual grouping benchmarks report IPv4 group calculation dropping from 518 ns to 307 ns without ASMap (approx. 40% reduction) and from 1,982 ns to 1,640 ns with ASMap (approx. 17% reduction) (PR description, commit 4131eaa53f).
result.scope_notes: The diff includes new benchmark targets and unit test coverage alongside the network and utility refactors.
result.card: This PR optimizes AddrMan address grouping and ASMap lookups by returning early when ASMap is unused, allocating lookup keys on the stack, simplifying ASN integer decoding, and reserving vector capacity. It targets CPU and allocation overhead in peer address ingestion, showing a measured 19.2% speedup in AddrManAdd and up to a 40% reduction in single-address grouping latency on a Raspberry Pi 5. It includes new benchmarks and tests for ASN parsing, with no open dependencies.
uncertainties: The code diff was not provided, though the commit log and benchmark tables provide detailed descriptions of each change.

risk.why: Flaws in address grouping or ASMap integer decoding could alter bucket placement in AddrMan, weakening peer diversity and eclipse resistance.
